Emerson.why: Its Ovation control systems automate power plants. Ovation orders rose 31% in Q3 FY2026 on what management calls unprecedented investment in power generation, including greenfield behind-the-meter power for data centers and new gas-fired capacity in North America, so the AI data-center power build-out lifts its orders and backlog.
Emerson.evidence: Emerson Q3 FY2026 (08-04-2026), CEO Lal Karsanbhai: 'We are seeing a continuation of the unprecedented investment in power generation with orders in our Ovation business up 31%.' COO Ram Krishnan: 'certainly in power, both on the generation side with Ovation, with fleet modernizations but also behind-the-meter opportunities driven by data centers and new capacity adds in North America there is significant penetration gains or participation gains we're driving.'

players.product: Ovation control systems for power plants (fleet modernizations, new gas-fired capacity and behind-the-meter generation for data centers); DeltaV Automation Platform for Data Centers (DeltaV DCS and PLCs controlling data-center thermal, mechanical and electrical sub-systems)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 (CEO Lal Karsanbhai, CFO Mike Baughman): underlying sales grew 6% (price contributed 3 points; MRO was 65% of sales), led by Test & Measurement and the Ovation business, both up 23%; underlying orders grew 7%, broad-based across all business groups and led by Software & Systems, up 10%. Growth verticals were up 27%, with semiconductor up 53% and power up 37%. Adjusted segment EBITDA margin expanded 140 basis points to 28.5%; adjusted EPS grew 13% to $1.71, above the top of guidance; free cash flow was $1.3 billion, up 36%, a 27.1% margin (helped by tariff refunds and tax-payment timing that shifted from Q3 to Q4). CEO: sales, margin expansion, earnings and cash all exceeded expectations.
quarterly_data.figure: underlying sales +6%; underlying orders +7%; adjusted segment EBITDA margin 28.5% (+140 bp); adjusted EPS $1.71 (+13%); free cash flow $1.3 billion (+36%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance raised (CEO, CFO): sales growth 5% (GAAP) with underlying growth of 3.5%; adjusted segment EBITDA margin still approximately 28%; adjusted EPS raised to approximately $6.55; free cash flow approximately $3.6 billion. Q4 FY2026: sales growth approximately 5% with minimal FX impact, adjusted segment EBITDA margin 28.5%, adjusted EPS approximately $1.85. CEO: the year is shaping up largely as expected, with a meaningful second-half step-up in organic growth and a slightly better Middle East than forecast in May. CFO: second-half underlying sales growth is accelerating as Emerson laps the software contract renewal dynamic and ships projects from a backlog that keeps growing year-over-year; stronger-than-expected U.S. growth has offset a slightly weaker China.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 sales +5% (underlying +3.5%); adjusted EPS ~$6.55; free cash flow ~$3.6 billion; Q4 adjusted EPS ~$1.85

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 segment outlook (CFO): Software & Systems raised to up 6% for the year (about 10% in Q4), with Test & Measurement raised to 14% and Control Systems & Software to 3.5% (including approximately 3 points of headwind from software renewals), both expected to grow 10% in Q4; software ACV growth still expected at 10% plus in 2026. Intelligent Devices: up 3% in Q4 and 2% for the year, supported by stable MRO with strength in the U.S. and growth verticals. Safety & Productivity: up 1% in Q4 and 2% for the year, with North America recovering and electric utilities strong but automotive and European markets weak. Long-range framework (COO Ram Krishnan): Software & Systems (Control Systems and T&M) is a 6% to 9% growth business and Intelligent Devices 3% to 6%; CFO: in an up cycle a business can run above that range, as T&M does this year (COO: about 14%).
quarterly_data.figure: Software & Systems +6% (T&M 14%, Control Systems & Software 3.5%); ACV growth 10% plus; long-range Software & Systems 6% to 9%

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog and project funnel (CFO, CEO, COO): backlog ended Q3 at $8.2 billion, up 7% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill of 1.0. The project funnel grew $1.2 billion to $12.4 billion, up 8% year-over-year; growth verticals were up $1 billion sequentially; the LNG funnel grew $350 million to $2.2 billion, with momentum across the Americas and the Middle East. Emerson won approximately $400 million from the funnel in Q3 (similar to Q2), 80% of it from growth verticals. CEO: the funnel is a three- to four-year view, with almost 1,000 individual projects across LNG and power alone; COO: most of the $12.4 billion is greenfield (brownfield modernizations are tracked separately).
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $8.2 billion (+7% Y/Y), book-to-bill 1.0; project funnel $12.4 billion (+8% Y/Y); LNG funnel $2.2 billion; Q3 funnel wins ~$400 million

quarterly_data.signal: Power (CEO, CFO): 'We are seeing a continuation of the unprecedented investment in power generation with orders in our Ovation business up 31%'; Ovation sales grew 23% and power sales 37% in Q3. Power rose $450 million in the project funnel from Q2 and now accounts for $3 billion of it. CEO: the power generation build-out is accelerating with substantial demand for both utility and behind-the-meter power, and the need for more stringent cybersecurity in critical infrastructure is leading customers to accelerate retrofit and upgrade programs. COO Ram Krishnan: beyond a strong market, Emerson is driving significant participation gains on the generation side with Ovation, in fleet modernizations, behind-the-meter opportunities driven by data centers and new capacity adds in North America.
quarterly_data.figure: Ovation orders +31%, sales +23%; power sales +37%; power funnel $3 billion (+$450 million vs Q2)

quarterly_data.signal: Ovation lead times (CEO Lal Karsanbhai): the Ovation order book now reaches into late 2027 and 2028 - 'We're sitting in the fourth quarter of '27, reaching into '28 at this point.'
quarterly_data.figure: Ovation lead times into Q4 2027, reaching into 2028

quarterly_data.signal: COO Ram Krishnan on the power mix: growth to date has been mostly fleet modernizations (brownfield), but in the quarter just ended and going into Q4 and early next year Emerson is starting to see new capacity coming online - gas-fired generation in North America will be a big part of the tailwind; the data center opportunity, which can be classified as behind-the-meter, is greenfield, as is much of the digital grid management (DGM) and nuclear power work - 'you're going to start seeing more of that in the numbers.'

Order (CEO): Emerson was selected by CFE, Mexico's largest power producer and national utility, to retrofit the control systems of a 2.1 gigawatt power plant with its Ovation control system, chosen for its proven ability to execute complex retrofits within accelerated timelines; the modernization supports CFE in meeting Mexico's growing power generation demand.

Order (CEO): China Nuclear Power Engineering Company, the design firm for the new Hualong-1 pressurized water reactor in Guangdong province (adding 2.4 gigawatts to China's nuclear installed base), chose Emerson to supply pressurizer pilot-operated safety valves for overpressure protection of the primary circuit, on its application expertise, nuclear qualifications and local presence.

Test & Measurement (CEO, CFO, COO): Q3 T&M sales up 23% and orders up 19% (above expectations), with semiconductor orders up 70% and double-digit growth in aerospace and defense and the portfolio business; semiconductor sales were up 53%. COO: a very strong market in RF and mixed-signal plus participation gains with new products. Win: Emerson will provide NI Semiconductor Test Systems to a leading Taiwan-based semiconductor manufacturer, improving test accuracy and consistency for critical components to help the customer capture AI-market opportunities. CEO: Emerson plays largely on the validation and production side rather than the laboratory, and remains 'relatively robust on semiconductors through 2027'.
quarterly_data.figure: T&M sales +23%, orders +19%; semiconductor orders +70%, sales +53%

quarterly_data.signal: Software (CEO, COO, CFO): software annual contract value (ACV) grew 9% year-over-year to $1.68 billion; ACV of AspenTech's digital grid management (DGM) suite grew 28% as electrification drives grid-modernization activity, and DGM continues to accelerate. COO expects to exit the year at better than 10% ACV growth as the software contract renewal dynamic reverses in Q4. Software & Systems margin was 31.8%, down 30 basis points, including a 1.5-point drag mainly from the renewal dynamic and a higher mix of lower-margin projects. CEO: cybersecurity spend is a significant driver of control-system upgrades in power generation and water systems and will remain one; none of the water facilities hit by the recent cyber attacks had an Emerson or Ovation control system.
quarterly_data.figure: ACV $1.68 billion (+9%); DGM ACV +28%; Software & Systems margin 31.8% (-30 bp)

quarterly_data.signal: Segments Q3 (CFO): Software & Systems underlying sales up 11% (Control Systems & Software up 7%), with significant growth in power, semiconductor and aerospace and defense. Intelligent Devices up 5%, better than expected on the Middle East and the timing of project shipments and sensors, with strength in power and LNG and growth in midstream gas and chemical (chemicals up, largely in the Final Control business; the U.S. and Middle East strong, China and Europe slow); margin 27.9%, up 240 basis points. Safety & Productivity up 2%, driven by electrical products and North American industrial activity, with European and automotive markets soft; margin 21.2%, up 80 basis points.
quarterly_data.figure: Software & Systems +11%; Intelligent Devices margin 27.9% (+240 bp); Safety & Productivity margin 21.2% (+80 bp)

quarterly_data.signal: Regions and Middle East (CFO, CEO, COO): Americas up 8% with the U.S. up 10% (Software & Systems up 14%, Intelligent Devices up 9%); Asia, Middle East and Africa up 8%, led by Middle East and Africa up 11%; China down 3% (improving, with sequential growth over Q2; COO expects low-single-digit growth in 2027); Europe down 1% with positive orders; demand strongest in the U.S., India, Japan and Southeast Asia. Middle East conflict: about a $25 million Q3 headwind versus February guidance with a similar Q4 impact, and approximately $100 million for FY2026 (about 0.5 point of revenue) as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed; field service engineers are back at pre-conflict levels but customer operational capacity is about 75%. CEO expects conditions to stay about the same in Q4 and perhaps into Q1 FY2027; new pipeline, storage and transportation projects are emerging, and large petrochemical and LNG field expansions in Qatar are expected to be released relatively quickly once a U.S.-Iran agreement brings certainty.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. +10%; Middle East and Africa +11%; Middle East conflict impact ~$100 million in FY2026 (~0.5 point of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Price, tariffs and MRO (CFO, COO, CEO): price-cost remains green, with full-year price tracking to about 2.5% (might round to 3%), and Q4 laps all tariff pricing. Emerson received $82 million of tariff refunds in Q3 (booked in cost of sales on a cash basis, excluded from adjusted results) and continues to file claims; COO: the net tariff benefit was largely eaten up by other inflation. CEO: MRO runs at about two-thirds of the business with no material change, though some shutdown and turnaround activity has been delayed because facilities are running hard. COO: pricing is better on modernizations than on greenfield, and better on MRO than on brownfield.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 price ~2.5%; tariff refunds $82 million in Q3
